concept.centerRule: Keep the physical setting and the action of each Scripture Scene primary; connections may reveal recurrence but may not erase changed context.

characterAnchors.label: God / the LORD
characterAnchors.note: Leads, speaks, provides, judges, prepares, and transforms in distinct wilderness passages.

characterAnchors.label: Hagar
characterAnchors.note: Appears in two early wilderness encounters.

characterAnchors.label: Israel
characterAnchors.note: Journeys, receives provision, resists, remembers, and is remembered.

characterAnchors.label: Moses
characterAnchors.note: Is called in wilderness terrain and leads Israel through it.

characterAnchors.label: David
characterAnchors.note: Uses wilderness strongholds while Saul pursues him.

characterAnchors.label: Elijah
characterAnchors.note: Enters the wilderness in exhaustion and continues toward Horeb.

characterAnchors.label: John the Baptist
characterAnchors.note: Appears as the wilderness voice in the Gospels.

characterAnchors.label: Jesus
characterAnchors.note: Is led into wilderness testing and later speaks about wilderness memory.

concept.throughline: From early journeys through Israel’s remembered testing, prophetic reversal, Gospel scenes, and Revelation, the wilderness recurs without becoming one fixed symbol.
